// Value bindings. A name BindVar registered reads like any other, and
// is writable only when the host bound it through Mutable.

// Reading an immutable binding: a constant and a sentinel.
assert.Equal(tb, "3600", fmt.Sprintf("%d", seconds(time.Hour)))
assert.Equal(tb, "EOF", message(io.EOF))

// Reading a mutable binding. The name is the variable, not a pointer
// to it, so this is a []string.
assert.Equal(tb, "prog", first(os.Args))
assert.Equal(tb, "2", fmt.Sprintf("%d", argc(os.Args)))

// & produces the pointer a *T parameter wants. Go's rule, spelled the
// way Go spells it: nothing auto-references an argument.
replace(&os.Args, "rewritten")
assert.Equal(tb, "rewritten", first(os.Args))
assert.Equal(tb, "1", fmt.Sprintf("%d", argc(os.Args)))

// Assignment writes the host's variable directly.
cursor = 41
bump(&cursor)
assert.Equal(tb, "42", fmt.Sprintf("%d", cursor))

// * reads through a pointer held by a program name.
p := ptrTo(7)
assert.Equal(tb, "7", fmt.Sprintf("%d", *p))
*p = 8
assert.Equal(tb, "8", fmt.Sprintf("%d", *p))
